title: Ideal Gas Law Simulator
tagline: Measure pressure from wall hits, then test P·A = N·T until it breaks
hub_blurb: Watch particles bounce in a box, measure pressure from the walls they hit, and test the ideal gas law against that measurement — then grow the particles and watch it drift.
card_blurb: A live kinetic-theory box: pressure is measured from the momentum the walls receive, temperature from the particles' energy, and the ideal gas law is a prediction the gauges test. Four guided experiments double N, double T, halve the box, and grow the particles until the law stops holding.
description: **Ideal Gas Law Simulator** — an offline two-dimensional kinetic-theory box. Hard discs fly, bounce off the walls and collide with each other; the pressure gauge adds up the momentum the walls receive and the temperature readout computes the particles' kinetic energy, so P·A = N·T is never typed in — it is a prediction the measurements test. Four guided predict-then-observe experiments (double N, double T, halve the box with a thermostat, grow the particles), a live speed histogram against the 2D Maxwell curve, a piston that heats the gas adiabatically when the thermostat is off, and automated sweeps that plot measured against predicted pressure.
